pairs.difference: A (popcorn cart): a loud red, white and gold cart on a saturated blue diamond backdrop. Its chroma fits the real cards, and the awning's white stripes stay fairly clean. B (station clock): the whole card is muted. The clock face is cream-yellow and the platform greens and teals are greyed. Subject chroma is 0.051, under the real range, and the card spreads across many weak hue families (6.64) instead of a few strong masses.
pairs.fix: Make the clock face clean white with a grey steel rim. Paint the station in clear, saturated green and teal so the background is as colourful as the real cards, and use fewer muddy in-between colours.

pairs.difference: A (duck rider): a saturated yellow duck with red and blue accents on a green burst. The shadow under the duck goes to a rust-brown, not more yellow. B (cactus): the ground is a solid saturated orange and the sky is a hot cyan burst, so the background is as loud as the green cactus. The cactus's shadow side is a single dark olive, and the warm sand carries no cool shadow.
pairs.fix: Paint the sand a pale sandy beige, not orange. Give the cactus's shadow side a cool blue-green, and give the shadow on the sand a soft violet tint.

pairs.difference: A (saddle): in the lens the seat, flaps and wooden rail are all one orange-brown family. The shadows only darken the orange and never shift toward maroon or purple, and the card has only 2.65 hue families, below the real range. This matches the generated baseball glove in the lessons. B (fountain): the stone reads as a cool grey neutral against the yellow stripes, with blue water as a clear second role. That matches how the real cards keep neutrals cool.
pairs.fix: Give the saddle leather a deep reddish-brown in its folds and under the seat, cooling toward plum in the darkest shadows. Make the wooden rail a paler, less saturated tan so it separates from the saddle.

pairs.difference: A (sneakers): many hues (blue, green, teal, pink, orange), but the white soles stay cool and the blue body holds a clear role against the orange and cream background. B (horseshoe): the grey metal is tinted warm beige by the magenta and orange surroundings, and warm share is 1.0, above the real range. Subject chroma is 0.031, far below the real range. The 'silver' reads as a beige blob between a hot magenta wall and an orange table.
pairs.fix: Paint the horseshoe as cool steel grey with bluish shadows and a white highlight. Make the table a calmer, darker brown so the whole card isn't pulled warm.

pairs.difference: A (sheriff star): the star, the ring and its balls are all one saturated gold. Shadows only drop to orange, so the subject is a single-hue mass, with the red gem as the only accent. B (beach umbrella): red and yellow panels against cyan rings, with the red shading to a deeper crimson. Both are close to real, so this call is weak.
pairs.fix: Shade the gold star toward a warm olive-brown in its recesses instead of plain orange, and keep pale cream highlights on the points and ring balls.

pairs.difference: A (covered wagon): the canvas cover is a warm cream, not a cool off-white, and its shadow chroma is 0.60, under the real range. The wagon wood, red wheels, green grass and blue sky all have roughly equal loudness, so the card has no resting neutral. B (dock and boat): mostly orange wood on cyan water, but the hull shadow turns red-maroon and the lily pads add a muted green, so its shadows stay rich.
pairs.fix: Paint the wagon's canvas as a cool off-white with soft blue-grey shadows. Tone the grass and sky down a little so the wagon is the most colourful thing on the card.

pairs.difference: A (flip-flops): coral soles with yellow straps on teal stripes. Two clear related hues, and the shadows keep their chroma (1.09). B (cowboy boots): both boots are one orange-brown leather, and the shadows only get darker within the same rust family. Shadow chroma is 0.739, just under the real range. The only accent is the gold spurs, which are also orange. This repeats the lesson's generated glove: an orange object with same-hue shadows on cyan.
pairs.fix: Draw the boots in a deeper chestnut-brown leather with cool plum-brown shadows in the creases and along the inner side. Make the stitching a pale cream, and the spurs a cooler, brighter steel-and-gold.

pairs.difference: A (scout jacket): a beige jacket, orange collar and cuffs, a dark green sash and yellow badges on green rays. The jacket's neutral beige rests the eye between the louder colours. B (cowboy hat): a single orange-tan felt mass whose shadows stay the same orange-rust. The only other colour is the red band. In the lens the whole hat is one or two flat brown bands against the blue, the same as the generated glove lesson.
pairs.fix: Paint the hat's felt as a muted tan with a darker brown-plum shadow under the brim and inside the crown dent. Add a pale cream highlight along the brim edge.

pairs.difference: A (diploma scroll): cream paper with a red ribbon and gold seal on deep blue. The paper's shadows shift to a dusty mauve, which is a related cool shadow. B (phone box): a pure red booth on an equally saturated lime green. Background chroma is 0.185, above the real range, so hero and background are equally loud and complementary, with no neutral. Its shadows are just darker red.
pairs.fix: Make the background a softer, slightly greyed green so the red booth is the loudest colour. Let the booth's shadow side shift toward a deep crimson-violet.

pairs.difference: A (dock post and life ring): saturated orange wood, a red-and-white ring and cyan water. Clear hue roles at real-card chroma. B (saloon): the building is a dusty grey-brown, with subject chroma at 0.057, near the bottom of the real range. The desert ground is beige, and only the small blue windows and red posts carry colour. Warm share is 0.689, above the real range. The card reads as muted and pulled warm, unlike the clean, loud local colours of the real cards.
pairs.fix: Paint the saloon's wood a clear warm brown with a few painted trim colours, such as a red or green sign board. Make the ground a lighter sand colour, and give the shadows a cool blue-violet tint.

pairs.difference: A (lasso): the rope is one orange-yellow hue and its shadows just darken toward brown-orange. The sand is beige, and the card has only 2.35 hue families, below the real range, with the small red band as the only accent. B (lawnmower): a red body, grey handle and black wheels on cyan and green, with clear hue roles. Its shadows are dull (0.406), but it keeps cool neutrals on the metal.
pairs.fix: Paint the rope as a pale straw-tan with cool brown-grey shadows between the coils. Keep the sand light and slightly cooler, and make the red binding the only bright accent.

pairs.difference: Both cards are warm desert sunsets, with warm share above the real range. A (campfire): the logs, tripod, rocks, ground and mesas all fall into one orange-brown family. The rocks are warm instead of grey, and in the lens almost everything is orange or brown. B (fuel pump): also warm, but it keeps cream-white trim, grey gauges and purple shadows on the pump's side.
pairs.fix: Paint the stones round the fire as cool grey, and the pot as a blue-black iron. Let the tripod's shadow sides cool toward violet so the fire's orange is the only hot area.

pattern: Generated cards pull warm. Neutrals that should be cool white or grey come out cream or beige: canvas, metal and stone. Orange and brown objects such as leather, rope, wood and felt are painted in one saturated orange hue whose shadows only get darker within that orange, instead of shifting to maroon, plum or blue-grey as on the real cards. The result is a subject that reads as one orange mass with too few hue families, and nothing neutral to rest the eye.
